==English==
{{wp|,+ (written)}}

===Alternative forms===
* {{l|en|coppy}}, {{l|en|coppie}}, {{l|en|copie}} {{qualifier|all obsolete}}

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈkɒpi/|a=RP}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈkɑpi/|a=GA}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-copy.ogg|a=US}}
* {{hyph|en|copy}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɒpi|s=2}}

===Etymology 1===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₃ep-}}
{{etymon|en|id=duplicate|:inh|enm:copy<id:duplicate>|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|copy}}, {{m|enm|copie}}, from {{der|en|fro|copie||abundance, plenty; transcript, copy}}, from {{der|en|la-med|copia||reproduction, transcript}}, from {{der|en|la|cōpia||plenty, abundance}}, from {{m|la|*coopia}}, from {{m|la|co-||together}} + {{m|la|ops||wealth, riches}}. More at {{l|en|opulent}}.

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}

# {{senseid|en|result of copying, a duplicate}} The result of copying; an identical or nearly identical duplicate of an [[original]].
#: {{ux|en|Please bring me at least 200 '''copies''' of this report. The photocopier is down the hall on the right.}}
#: {{ux|en|His new book is out. I have a signed '''copy'''. He'll send you a '''copy''' if you want one. He's giving free '''copies''' to his former colleagues who want one. The press run is 3000 '''copies''', and he hopes to sell more press runs after this one.}}
#: {{ux|en|I already saw their draft. She emailed me a '''copy''' yesterday. I can forward it to you so that you have your own '''copy'''.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1656|author={{w|John Denham (poet)|John Denham}}|title=preface to The Destruction of Troy
|passage=I have not the vanity to think my '''copy''' equal to the original.}}
## {{senseid|en|result of gene or chromosomal duplication}} {{lb|en|genetics}} The result of gene or chromosomal duplication.
##: {{ux|en|Every cell in this organism contains a '''copy''' of each gene, but whether that copy will be expressed depends on complex factors of cell differentiation and epigenetics.}}
# {{senseid|en|an imitation, sometimes an inferior one}} An [[imitation]], sometimes of inferior quality.
#: {{ux|en|That handbag is a '''copy'''. You can tell because the buckle is different.}}
# {{senseid|en|text that is to be typeset or similarly prepared and published}} {{lb|en|typesetting|journalism|publishing}} The [[text#Noun|text]] (words, [[content#Noun|content]]) that is to be [[typeset]] or similarly prepared and [[publish]]ed.
#: {{ux|en|This organization doesn't publish any copy that hasn't been edited by a good '''copy''' editor.}}
## {{senseid|en|output of copywriters, as marketing or advertising matter}} {{lb|en|marketing|advertising}} The output of [[copywriter]]s, who are employed to write material which encourages [[consumers]] to buy goods or services.
##: {{co|en|ad '''copy'''; advertising '''copy'''}}
## {{lb|en|uncountable}} The text to be set into [[newspaper]] articles, [[magazine]] pages, or similar.
##: {{ux|en|Submit all '''copy''' to the appropriate editor.}}
# {{senseid|en|person employed to carry copy and run errands}} {{lb|en|journalism}} A person employed to carry copy and run errands.
#: {{hypo|en|copy boy}}
# {{senseid|en|schoolwork pad or workbook}} A [[schoolwork]] [[pad#Noun|pad]] or [[workbook]].
#: {{ux|en|Tim got in trouble for forgetting his maths '''copy'''.}}
# {{senseid|en|particular instance of a book, a printed impression or digital file}} A particular [[instance]] of a [[book]]: a single printed impression or digital file representing it.
#: {{ux|en|Our town's public library has several '''copies''' of the Bible, in each of several editions.}}
#: {{ux|en|Our town's public library has several '''copies''' of the second edition of Smith's textbook, but it doesn't yet have any '''copies''' of any newer edition.}}
# {{senseid|en|instance of a particular issue of a periodical}} A particular [[instance]] of an [[issue]] of a [[periodical#Noun|periodical]] (e.g., [[magazine]], [[journal]], [[bulletin]]): a single printed impression or digital file representing that issue; {{lb|en|metonymically}} the [[issue#Noun|issue]].
#: {{ux|en|Have you seen the latest '''copy''' of ''Newsweek'' yet?}}
# {{senseid|en|paper size}} {{lb|en|archaic}} Writing paper of a particular size: {{syn of|en|bastard<id:paper size>}}.
# {{senseid|en|pattern, model, or example, obsoletely}} {{lb|en|obsolete}} That which is to be imitated, transcribed, or reproduced; a pattern, model{{,}} or example.
#: {{ux|en|His virtues are an excellent '''copy''' for imitation.}}
#* {{RQ:Holder Speech|passage=Let him first learn to write, after a '''copy''' of all the letters.}}
# {{senseid|en|abundance or plenty, obsoletely}} {{lb|en|obsolete}} An [[abundance]] or [[plenty]] of anything.
#* {{RQ:Jonson Every Man out of His Humour|act=II|scene=i|sig=F|verso=1|page=49|passage=[S]he was bleſt with no more '''Copie''' of wit, but to ſerue his Humor thus.}}
# {{senseid|en|copyhold, tenure, or lease, obsoletely}} {{lb|en|obsolete}} [[copyhold]]; [[tenure]]; [[lease]].
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Macbeth|3|2|passage=But in them nature's '''copy''''s not eterne}}

===Etymology 2===
{{etymon|en|id=to duplicate|:inh|enm:copien<id:to duplicate>|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|copien}}, from {{der|en|fro|copier}} and {{der|en|la-med|cōpiō}}.<ref>{{R:MED Online|entry=cō̆pīen|pos=v|id=MED9661}}</ref>

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To produce an object identical to a given object.
#: {{ux|en|Please '''copy''' these reports for me.}}
#: {{ux|en|Don't '''copy''' that floppy!}}
#* {{RQ:Economist|date=2014-06-21|volume=411|issue=8892| title=[http://www.economist.com/news/books-and-arts/21604535-real-sir-isaac-newton-was-not-first-king-reason-last Magician’s brain]| passage=[Isaac Newton] was obsessed with alchemy. He spent hours '''copying''' alchemical recipes and trying to replicate them in his laboratory. He believed that the Bible contained numerological codes. The truth is that Newton was very much a product of his time.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To give or transmit a copy to (a person).
#: {{ux|en|[[make sure|Make sure]] you '''copy''' me on that important memo.}}
#: {{ux|en|All heads of departments have been '''copied'''.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|computing}} To place a copy of an object in memory for later use.
#: {{ux|en|First '''copy''' the files, and then paste them in another directory.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To imitate.
#: {{ux|en|Don't '''copy''' my dance moves.}}
#: {{ux|en|Mom, he's '''copying''' me!}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1793|author=w:Dugald Stewart|title=Outlines of Moral Philosophy
|passage=We '''copy''' instinctively the voices of our companions, their accents, and their modes of pronunciation.}}
# {{lb|en|radio}} To receive a transmission successfully.
#: {{ux|en|Do you '''copy'''?}}
